answer.sql: WITH latest_recommend AS (SELECT facility_id, measure_id, measure_name, score FROM (SELECT mv.facility_id, mv.measure_id, mv.measure_name, mv.score, ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY mv.facility_id, mv.measure_id ORDER BY mv.period_end DESC NULLS LAST) AS rn FROM hq.measure_values AS mv WHERE UPPER(mv.measure_id) = UPPER('H_RECMND_DY') AND mv.score IS NOT NULL) AS ranked WHERE rn = 1) SELECT h.hospital_ownership AS ownership_type, COUNT(*) AS hospital_count, 'H_RECMND_DY' AS measure_id, 'Patients who reported YES, they would definitely recommend the hospital' AS measure_name, ROUND(CAST(AVG(lr.score) AS DECIMAL), 2) AS avg_would_definitely_recommend_pct, ROUND(CAST(AVG(h.overall_rating) AS DECIMAL), 2) AS avg_overall_star_rating FROM hq.hospitals AS h LEFT JOIN latest_recommend AS lr ON lr.facility_id = h.facility_id WHERE UPPER(h.state) = UPPER('TX') GROUP BY h.hospital_ownership HAVING COUNT(*) >= 5 ORDER BY avg_would_definitely_recommend_pct DESC NULLS LAST, ownership_type LIMIT 200

answer.answer: For the “patients who rated the hospital 9 or 10” measure, 297 Texas hospitals had a score. The largest number of reporting periods for any one hospital was 1, and 0 hospitals had scores from more than one period, so none had multiple periods for comparing changes.
answer.sql: WITH hospital_periods AS (SELECT h.facility_id, COUNT(DISTINCT (mv.period_start, mv.period_end)) AS reporting_periods FROM hq.hospitals AS h JOIN hq.measure_values AS mv ON mv.facility_id = h.facility_id WHERE UPPER(h.state) = UPPER('TX') AND UPPER(mv.measure_id) = UPPER('H_HSP_RATING_9_10') AND mv.score IS NOT NULL GROUP BY h.facility_id) SELECT 'H_HSP_RATING_9_10' AS measure_id, 'Patients who gave their hospital a rating of 9 or 10 on a scale from 0 (lowest) to 10 (highest)' AS measure_name, COUNT(*) AS texas_hospitals_with_a_score, MAX(reporting_periods) AS largest_number_of_reporting_periods, COUNT(*) FILTER(WHERE reporting_periods > 1) AS hospitals_with_more_than_one_period FROM hospital_periods LIMIT 200

h.readm_score) / NULLIF(s.readm_sd, 0) + (h.recommend_score - s.recommend_avg) / NULLIF(s.recommend_sd, 0) + (h.sepsis_score - s.sepsis_avg) / NULLIF(s.sepsis_sd, 0)) / 3, 2) AS composite FROM hospital_scores AS h CROSS JOIN stats AS s WHERE h.readm_score IS NOT NULL AND h.recommend_score IS NOT NULL AND h.sepsis_score IS NOT NULL), top_ranked AS (SELECT *, ROW_NUMBER() OVER (ORDER BY composite DESC, facility_name, county) AS position FROM composites), bottom_ranked AS (SELECT *, ROW_NUMBER() OVER (ORDER BY composite ASC, facility_name, county) AS position FROM composites) SELECT group_name, facility_name, county, composite FROM (SELECT 'Highest' AS group_name, facility_name, county, composite, 1 AS group_order, position FROM top_ranked WHERE position <= 10 UNION ALL SELECT 'Lowest' AS group_name, facility_name, county, composite, 2 AS group_order, position FROM bottom_ranked WHERE position <= 10) AS ranked ORDER BY group_order, position LIMIT 200

records.question: For six measures, what share of Texas hospitals do better than the national average (average over all U.S. hospitals with a score)? Measures: 30-day pneumonia readmission rate, 30-day heart failure death rate, central-line infection ratio (lower is better for these three), sepsis care percentage, 'would definitely recommend' percentage and HCAHPS summary star rating (higher is better for these three). Return measure ID, the national average (2 decimals), Texas hospitals with a score, how many beat the national average and the share in percent (1 decimal), highest share first, ties by measure ID.

answer.question: For six measures, what share of Texas hospitals do better than the national average (average over all U.S. hospitals with a score)? Measures: 30-day pneumonia readmission rate, 30-day heart failure death rate, central-line infection ratio (lower is better for these three), sepsis care percentage, 'would definitely recommend' percentage and HCAHPS summary star rating (higher is better for these three). Return measure ID, the national average (2 decimals), Texas hospitals with a score, how many beat the national average and the share in percent (1 decimal), highest share first, ties by measure ID.
answer.answer: From highest share to lowest: HAI_1_SIR — national average 0.58; 151 Texas hospitals with a score, 99 beat the average (65.6%). MORT_30_HF — 11.07; 206 with a score, 132 beat it (64.1%). SEP_1 — 63.79; 233 with a score, 146 beat it (62.7%). READM_30_PN — 17.34; 258 with a score, 150 beat it (58.1%). H_RECMND_DY — 71.22; 297 with a score, 158 beat it (53.2%). H_STAR_RATING — 3.27; 229 with a score, 92 beat it (40.2%).
answer.sql: WITH targets AS (SELECT * FROM (VALUES ('READM_30_PN', FALSE), ('MORT_30_HF', FALSE), ('HAI_1_SIR', FALSE), ('SEP_1', TRUE), ('H_RECMND_DY', TRUE), ('H_STAR_RATING', TRUE)) AS t(measure_id, higher_is_better)), ranked AS (SELECT UPPER(mv.measure_id) AS measure_id, mv.facility_id, h.state, mv.score, ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY mv.facility_id, UPPER(mv.measure_id) ORDER BY mv.period_end DESC NULLS LAST, mv.period_start DESC NULLS LAST) AS rn FROM hq.measure_values AS mv JOIN hq.hospitals AS h ON h.facility_id = mv.facility_id JOIN targets AS t ON UPPER(mv.measure_id) = t.measure_id WHERE mv.score IS NOT NULL), latest AS (SELECT measure_id, facility_id, state, score FROM ranked WHERE rn = 1), national AS (SELECT measure_id, AVG(score) AS national_avg FROM latest GROUP BY measure_id), texas AS (SELECT l.measure_id, COUNT(*) AS texas_hospitals_with_score, COUNT(*) FILTER(WHERE (t.higher_is_better AND l.score > n.national_avg) OR (NOT t.higher_is_better AND l.score < n.national_avg)) AS texas_hospitals_beating_national FROM latest AS l JOIN national AS n ON n.measure_id = l.measure_id JOIN targets AS t ON t.measure_id = l.measure_id WHERE UPPER(l.state) = 'TX' GROUP BY l.measure_id) SELECT n.measure_id, m.measure_name, ROUND(CAST(n.national_avg AS DECIMAL), 2) AS national_average, tx.texas_hospitals_with_score, tx.texas_hospitals_beating_national, ROUND(100.0 * tx.texas_hospitals_beating_national / NULLIF(tx.texas_hospitals_with_score, 0), 1) AS share_percent FROM national AS n JOIN texas AS tx ON tx.measure_id = n.measure_id JOIN hq.measures AS m ON UPPER(m.measure_id) = n.measure_id ORDER BY share_percent DESC, n.measure_id LIMIT 200
